coordinate_basis: Placed by distance along the Historic Green River Road as OpenStreetMap draws it (S39), counted from the south-east end of the Battlefield Trail loop (35.13294, -81.81012), where the staff ride's Vantage 6 (S95, p. 77) and the NPS wayside "The British Army" (S105) put the head of Tarleton's column as it came onto the field. 565 m up the road, at the bend: about 85 m behind the first position. Morgan says "about fifty paces" (S96), Thomas "aboutt 80 yards" (S101), Howard "about 100 yards" (S98); the staff ride walks 100 m from Vantage 8 to Vantage 10 (S95, p. 82), and the NPS handbook puts the deciding fight "just beyond the bend in the road" (S104, p. 88). See CH08.
source_wording: S96: "We retired in good order about fifty paces, formed, and advanced on the enemy, and gave them a fortunate volley". S98 (Howard): Morgan "ordered me to retreat to Washington's horse about 100 yards, and there form ... The enemy pressed upon us in rather disorder ... They were by this time within 30 yards of us with two field pieces".
notes: The line kept its order as it fell back (S98); the parts are drawn as in the first position.

source_wording: S97: "at three o'clock in the morning on the 17th, the pickets being called in, the British troops ... were directed to follow the route the Americans had taken the previous evening ... Before dawn, Thickelle creek was passed, when an advanced guard of cavalry was ordered to the front." S96: an hour before daylight Tarleton "had advanced within five miles of our camp".
notes: Mackenzie has the march begin at two o'clock (S102): CH13. 24 Nov 2026: shown 06:16 to 06:22 (was 06:20 to 06:28), so the column sets off with its advance guard and marches the 3.1 km to the field at about 6 km/h.

activity: On the left flank of the line
place_description: Left of the 7th Regiment
coordinate_basis: Placed by distance along the Historic Green River Road as OpenStreetMap draws it (S39), counted from the south-east end of the Battlefield Trail loop (35.13294, -81.81012), where the staff ride's Vantage 6 (S95, p. 77) and the NPS wayside "The British Army" (S105) put the head of Tarleton's column as it came onto the field. The line of battle is 85 m short of that point (at -85 m) and square to the road: Bearss's Plate I draws it 292 m (320 yards) in front of the skirmish line (205 m up the road), and his text has it close "to within 300 yards of Morgan's skirmish line" (S107, p. 17). Tarleton's own "within three hundred yards of the enemy" (S97) fits it. Morgan's "four hundred yards in front of our advanced corps" (S96) would put it 75 m further back, and the NPS wayside "Form the Line of Battle" 220 m further forward (CH16). Each unit has its share of about 340 yards by its strength (S95, p. 91), in Tarleton's order from right to left.
source_wording: S97: "A captain, with fifty dragoons, was placed on each flank of the corps, who formed the British front line, to protect their own, and threaten the flanks of the enemy". S95, p. 76: "On the extreme left flank stood two troops of British Legion cavalry under Captain Ogilvie."
notes: Audit of 24 Nov 2026: moved back with the British line (CH16). Which flank Ogilvie held is disputed (CH17).

activity: Line of battle
place_description: British line, the right of the line
coordinate_basis: Placed by distance along the Historic Green River Road as OpenStreetMap draws it (S39), counted from the south-east end of the Battlefield Trail loop (35.13294, -81.81012), where the staff ride's Vantage 6 (S95, p. 77) and the NPS wayside "The British Army" (S105) put the head of Tarleton's column as it came onto the field. The line of battle is 85 m short of that point (at -85 m) and square to the road: Bearss's Plate I draws it 292 m (320 yards) in front of the skirmish line (205 m up the road), and his text has it close "to within 300 yards of Morgan's skirmish line" (S107, p. 17). Tarleton's own "within three hundred yards of the enemy" (S97) fits it. Morgan's "four hundred yards in front of our advanced corps" (S96) would put it 75 m further back, and the NPS wayside "Form the Line of Battle" 220 m further forward (CH16). Each unit has its share of about 340 yards by its strength (S95, p. 91), in Tarleton's order from right to left.
source_wording: S97: "The light infantry were then ordered to file to the right till they became equal to the flank of the American front line: The legion infantry were added to their left; and, under the fire of a 3-pounder, this part of the British troops was instructed to advance within three hundred yards of the enemy. This situation being acquired, the 7th regiment was commanded to form upon the left of the legion infantry, and the other 3-pounder was given to the right division of the 7th". S96: "The enemy drew up in single line of battle, four hundred yards in front of our advanced corps."
notes: Audit of 24 Nov 2026: moved back 155 m (from 70 m up the road), and overall `medium` to `low`. See CH16.

activity: Broken; lays down its arms
place_description: British line, the right of the line
coordinate_basis: Placed by distance along the Historic Green River Road as OpenStreetMap draws it (S39), counted from the south-east end of the Battlefield Trail loop (35.13294, -81.81012), where the staff ride's Vantage 6 (S95, p. 77) and the NPS wayside "The British Army" (S105) put the head of Tarleton's column as it came onto the field. source_wording: S97: "an unaccountable panic extended itself along the whole line." S101 (McJunkin): "One battalion throws down their arms and the men fall to the earth. Another commences flight, but Washington darts before them with his cavalry and they too ground their arms." S96: "five hundred and two non-commissioned officers and privates prisoners".
notes: The unit is assumed to have kept its place in the line as it went forward. Audit of 24 Nov 2026: moved back 95 m (from 455 m), after Bearss. It now lies about 30 m from wayside 13030, which stays as the second witness. 24 Nov 2026, Morgan's review: drawn until 07:56, not 08:30. The unit surrendered here; like the guns it is then taken off the map instead of standing in line in front of the Americans. The reading and its times are unchanged.

coordinate_basis: Placed by distance along the Historic Green River Road as OpenStreetMap draws it (S39), counted from the south-east end of the Battlefield Trail loop (35.13294, -81.81012), where the staff ride's Vantage 6 (S95, p. 77) and the NPS wayside "The British Army" (S105) put the head of Tarleton's column as it came onto the field. About 360 m up the road: Bearss has the light infantry, the Legion infantry and the 7th overtaken and surrendering "about 200 yards from the point of disaster" (S107, p. 21), counted here from where Howard's volley struck them (538 m). source_wording: S97: "an unaccountable panic extended itself along the whole line." S101 (McJunkin): "One battalion throws down their arms and the men fall to the earth. Another commences flight, but Washington darts before them with his cavalry and they too ground their arms." S96: "five hundred and two non-commissioned officers and privates prisoners".
notes: The unit is assumed to have kept its place in the line as it went forward. Audit of 24 Nov 2026: moved back 95 m (from 455 m), after Bearss. It now lies about 30 m from wayside 13030, which stays as the second witness. 24 Nov 2026, Morgan's review: drawn until 07:56, not 08:30. The unit surrendered here; like the guns it is then taken off the map instead of standing in line in front of the Americans. The reading and its times are unchanged.

activity: In reserve
place_description: About 150 yards behind the left of the 7th Regiment
coordinate_basis: Placed by distance along the Historic Green River Road as OpenStreetMap draws it (S39), counted from the south-east end of the Battlefield Trail loop (35.13294, -81.81012), where the staff ride's Vantage 6 (S95, p. 77) and the NPS wayside "The British Army" (S105) put the head of Tarleton's column as it came onto the field. The line of battle is 85 m short of that point (at -85 m) and square to the road: Bearss's Plate I draws it 292 m (320 yards) in front of the skirmish line (205 m up the road), and his text has it close "to within 300 yards of Morgan's skirmish line" (S107, p. 17). Tarleton's own "within three hundred yards of the enemy" (S97) fits it. Morgan's "four hundred yards in front of our advanced corps" (S96) would put it 75 m further back, and the NPS wayside "Form the Line of Battle" 220 m further forward (CH16). Each unit has its share of about 340 yards by its strength (S95, p. 91), in Tarleton's order from right to left. The 71st is 137 m (150 yards) behind that line and reaching a little beyond its left.
source_wording: S97: "the 1st battalion of the 71st was desired to extend a little to the left of the 7th regiment, and to remain one hundred and fifty yards in the rear. This body of infantry, and near two hundred cavalry, composed the reserve."
notes: Mackenzie has the reserve not yet clear of the woods when the attack began (S102; S95, p. 58). Audit of 24 Nov 2026: moved back with the British line (CH16), and both confidences `medium` to `low`: Hanger says the 71st was "but 300 yards" behind (S95, p. 159 n. 29), Mackenzie that it "remained near a mile distant" (S102, in S95 p. 152), and Bearss that the reserve "was about a mile away" when Tarleton sent for it (S107, p. 19). See CH14.

activity: Reconnoitres and forms the line

coordinate_basis: Placed by distance along the Historic Green River Road as OpenStreetMap draws it (S39), counted from the south-east end of the Battlefield Trail loop (35.13294, -81.81012), where the staff ride's Vantage 6 (S95, p. 77) and the NPS wayside "The British Army" (S105) put the head of Tarleton's column as it came onto the field. The line of battle is 85 m short of that point (at -85 m) and square to the road: Bearss's Plate I draws it 292 m (320 yards) in front of the skirmish line (205 m up the road), and his text has it close "to within 300 yards of Morgan's skirmish line" (S107, p. 17). Tarleton's own "within three hundred yards of the enemy" (S97) fits it. Morgan's "four hundred yards in front of our advanced corps" (S96) would put it 75 m further back, and the NPS wayside "Form the Line of Battle" 220 m further forward (CH16). Each unit has its share of about 340 yards by its strength (S95, p. 91), in Tarleton's order from right to left. Tarleton is drawn 30 m behind the centre of the line.
source_wording: S97: "He discovered that the American commander had formed a front line of about one thousand militia, and had composed his second line and reserve of five hundred continental light infantry, one hundred and twenty of Washington's cavalry, and three hundred back woodsmen."
notes: Where Tarleton himself stood is not recorded: drawn behind the centre of his line. Audit of 24 Nov 2026: moved back with the British line (CH16).
